title: Repository facts
description: What `tools/facts.py` writes: counts and names that describe a repository, taken with the engine's own inventory and detection, with no verdict. The file holds no time, no absolute path, no machine or user name and no file content, so one repository state gives one file. IN DEVELOPMENT: until the tool writes every section, only `facts_version` and `label` are required. Field semantics and the caps are in SCHEMA.md.

facts_version.description: Version of this schema. 0.x versions may break between releases; consumers refuse a version they do not know.

label.description: The repository's short name, derived from the name of the target directory by the rule that names output files. It is the same pattern as `repo_label` in the intake.

git.description: The repository state the facts describe. From the engine's target module.

sha.description: The commit at HEAD, in full; null when the target is not a git repository or has no commit.

dirty.description: Whether `git status --porcelain` listed anything. False for a target that is not a git repository.

inventory.description: What the engine's walk of the target found. The counts are those of `audit.scan.build_inventory` for the same target and options.

by_kind.description: Files inspected, per `audit.scan.Kind`. Every kind is present, with 0 when there is none.

skipped.description: Paths the walk left out, counted per reason and never listed. Only reasons that occurred, sorted by reason. The reasons are the engine's own words, such as `ignored` and `symlink`.

truncated.description: Whether `--max-files` stopped the walk, so that every count is a lower bound.

excludes.description: The `--exclude` globs, as given and in the order given, up to the cap in `caps.excludes`. A glob that is not printable ASCII or is over 100 characters is not listed and is counted in `omitted`.

stack.description: What `audit.stack.detect_stack` recognised. Every list is sorted. A repository the engine does not recognise gives empty lists and a note. Each list is bounded by the engine's own table of names, so none has a cut in `caps`.

ecosystems.description: Ecosystems named by a manifest, or recognised from source files.

source_only.description: The ecosystems in `ecosystems` that were recognised from source files because no manifest names them. Such a project declares no dependencies.

package_managers.description: Package managers, named by their lockfiles or manifests.

ci_providers.description: CI providers, named by their configuration files.

test_frameworks.description: Test frameworks, named by their configuration or layout.

hook_managers.description: Git hook managers, named by their configuration.

notes.description: The engine's own notes on what it could not recognise, as it wrote them.

instruction_files.description: The instruction files of the engine's variants table that are present, sorted by path, up to the cap in `caps.instruction_files`. A file whose path is not printable ASCII or is over 128 characters is not listed and is counted in `omitted`. It says nothing about whether a file is good, canonical or a stub.

variant.description: The variants table's name for the file's family.

components.description: What `audit.components.detect_components` found. The implicit root component is not listed.

declared.description: Components that a manifest declares, sorted by path, up to the cap in `caps.declared_components`. A component whose name or path is not printable ASCII, or is too long, is not listed and is counted in `omitted`.

declared_by.description: The manifest and the key that declared it, as the engine names them.

manifest.description: The component's own build manifest; null when it has none.

candidates.description: Paths that look like components but that no manifest declares, sorted, up to the cap in `caps.candidate_components`. Informational only.

notes.description: The engine's own notes on the component model, as it wrote them.

size.description: How large the repository is, by the engine's file count. The thresholds the class used are in the file, so a reader sees the rule.

class.description: `small` below `small_below` files, `medium` below `medium_below`, `large` below `large_below`, and `huge` from there on or when the walk was cut short.

caps.description: The cut each list that depends on the repository or on the operator has, and how many entries it left out. `omitted` counts entries beyond the limit and entries that do not fit the field rules. A list that the engine's own tables bound has no entry.

token.description: A name from one of the engine's tables: lower case letters, digits and a few separators.

label_text.description: A short name that the engine or the repository gives: printable ASCII.

glob.description: A path glob given by the operator: printable ASCII.

relpath.description: A path relative to the repository root, in POSIX form, printable ASCII. It never starts with a slash or with a drive letter.
